classification.difficultyReason: Combines symbolic rectilinear lengths, perimeter and composite area, then factorises the area to obtain an equivalent square.

content.prompt:
A swimming pool is designed in an L-shape with dimensions in metres as shown.

The pool is enlarged or reduced depending on the value of $x$.

spec.sourceRegion: Challenge exercise question 7, L-shaped pool at right
spec.description: Unshaded orthogonal L-shaped pool with boundary vertices A, B, C, D, E, F in order. AB is the inward horizontal step, BC rises to the upper edge, DE is the full height, and EF is the full width. Coordinates express topology and approximate source proportions, not numerical lengths.
spec.mathematics: AB=x+9, BC=2x, DE=3x+9, EF=2x+16; all dimensions are in metres.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and vertex names are visible; missing lengths and calculated results are absent.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the area of the swimming pool in terms of $x$. Expand and simplify your answer.

answer.short:
$(4x^2+48x+144)\text{ m}^2$.

Subtract the missing upper-left rectangle from the enclosing rectangle.
answer.worked:
The enclosing rectangle has width $2x+16$ and height $3x+9$. The missing upper-left rectangle has width $x+9$ and height $2x$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=(2x+16)(3x+9)-2x(x+9)\\A&=6x^2+66x+144-(2x^2+18x)\\A&=(4x^2+48x+144)\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: It is decided that a square swimming pool would be a better use of space.

children.label: i
children.prompt: By factorising your answer to part d, find the dimensions, in terms of $x$, of a square swimming pool with the same area as the L-shaped swimming pool.

answer.short:
$(2x+12)\text{ m}\times(2x+12)\text{ m}$.

Factorise the area as $(2x+12)^2$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A&=4(x^2+12x+36)\\A&=4(x+6)^2\\A&=(2x+12)^2\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
The square has side length $(2x+12)\text{ m}$, so its dimensions are $(2x+12)\text{ m}\times(2x+12)\text{ m}$.
